response:
It is completely normal to feel nervous and shaky, even after a couple of sessions. Therapy involves opening up about vulnerable and personal topics, which can naturally trigger anxiety. Building trust with a therapist takes time, and your mind and body are still adjusting to this new, unfamiliar environment. There is no set timeline for when you "should" feel completely relaxed, so try not to put pressure on yourself to feel perfectly calm right away. 

You might find it helpful to tell your therapist exactly how you are feeling when you walk in. They are trained to help you navigate this anxiety and can adjust the pace of the session to make you feel more comfortable. Be patient with yourself and recognize that continuing to show up, even when you feel anxious, shows a lot of courage.
